text: Turing's imitation game (the Turing test) proposes that machine intelligence be assessed by...
choices: whether an interrogator can reliably distinguish the machine from a human in a blind text conversation
whether the machine's internal processes are biologically implemented
whether the machine sincerely reports having conscious experiences
explanation: Turing replaced 'Can machines think?' with a behavioral, third-person test of conversational indistinguishability, explicitly bracketing inner experience and substrate. Phi is IIT's criterion, biological implementation is Searle's requirement, and self-reported consciousness is exactly what Turing set aside as untestable.
